reason: The text extensively features regular people characters with significant dialogue, emotions, and expressed opinions. The Israelites collectively speak multiple times (Exodus 19:8 קוֹל אֶחָד 'in one voice'; 20:19 requesting Moses mediate rather than God speak directly; 24:7 'all that the Lord has spoken we will do'). Aaron, a named character, has dialogue explaining and defending the people's actions. Emotions are prominent throughout: the people experience fear and trembling (וַיֶּחֱרַד כָּל־ הָעָם 19:16; וַיַּרְא הָעָם וַיָּנֻעוּ 20:18), willingness and obedience, and engage in celebration. The people express opinions about their preferences (wanting Moses as intermediary rather than direct divine communication) and Aaron voices explanations for the people's behavior (אַתָּה יָדַעְתָּ אֶת־ הָעָם כִּי בְרָע הוּא 32:22). These are not mere background figures but active participants with agency, voice, and emotional/psychological substance.
